facts.value: 6 Treasury Management Strategy Statement 2026/27 (Appendix 4 to the covering Q3 Treasury Management Report), to Council on 26 February 2026. Read alongside its companion the 6 Treasury Management Report (Q3 2025/26 performance + AIS 2026/27, doc 50127114), which sits on the same agenda and carries the loan/investment tables, portfolio detail, MUFG 22.12.25 rate view, pooled-fund return history and the borrowing narrative. Everything below is machine-checked against the saved text of both papers.

facts.note: Strategy p.8. Movement in CFR of +£175.6m across the three-year strategy period is the whole story here — nearly a tripling of underlying indebtedness driven by £181.7m of net financing need (67.6 + 65.9 + 48.2) less £10.4m of MRP. Note the second table on p.12 shows a row labelled 'The Capital Financing Requirement' with different (smaller) figures — those numbers equal external debt + OLTL for each year, not the true CFR. The p.8 numbers are authoritative; see extract §7.

Per Strategy §1.2.2 (p.4), quarterly treasury reports (end of June / end of December) go to the Executive, Resources and Contracts Policy Development and Scrutiny Committee; Q4 2025/26 has already been presented (June 2026 and Council 6 July 2026). summary.text:
A distinctive shape in the library: Bromley has no external borrowing today — PWLB £0, LOBOs £0, local authorities £0 — and is about to have a lot. £273m has been agreed in principle with the PWLB (Strategy §2.2) and the scheduled drawdown reaches £241.4m by 31 March 2029: £127.3m in 2026/27, £65.9m in 2027/28, £48.2m in 2028/29. The CFR nearly triples over the strategy period, from £90.9m to £266.5m. The ratio of financing costs to net revenue moves from zero to 2.2% inside three years.

Our loan-book reconciliation is unusual because it is empty on both sides. `price_book.py --find "Bromley"` returns only DOWNEND & BROMLEY HEATH PC (S GLOS), a South Gloucestershire parish council; there is no PWLB borrower entity for the London Borough. The paper's p.11 table agrees: PWLB £0, LOBOs £0, LAs £0. Two independent records tie to zero, which is the sentence the email leads with. The balance-sheet identity holds every year (CFR − external − OLTL = internal): today's £53–63m of internal borrowing collapses to £1–3m by 2027 as PWLB displaces the reserves-funded portion of historic capital spend.

The operative event is imminent. Q3 §7.1 targets first drawdown 'from September 2026' on the expectation that 50-year PWLB falls from about 5.91% (November 2025) to 5.40% by March 2026 and 5.30% from September 2026, per MUFG's 22.12.25 forecast. Actual today (14 August 2026) is 6.27% at 50 years — 87 bps above the Sep-26 forecast and 36 bps above the Nov-25 starting point that framed the timetable. The whole long end is 85–105 bps above forecast at every tenor. Their target borrowing rate 'now' (Strategy p.14, end Q2 2027) of 5.20% at 50 years would require the long end to fall about 107 bps over the next ten months.

Portfolio side is active and distinctive. £257.2m of investments as at 31/12/25, of which £55m sits with five other councils at 4.30–4.75% — more LA-to-LA than bank deposits on the book. £100m in three pooled funds (CCLA property £40m, Fidelity multi-asset £40m, Schroders diversified £20m) with an Income Equalisation reserve now at £18.6m to absorb capital-value volatility when the IFRS 9 override ends 31 March 2029. Portfolio total return YTD 2025/26 6.22%, of which alternatives 8.96%, core 4.41%. Interest budget falls from £8.2m (2025/26) to £4.96m (2026/27) on lower Bank Rate and depleting balances.

Officer address is on the Q3 report cover: Abdul Munim, Principal Accountant. Peter Turner is the Chief Officer (Director of Finance) but no email is published for him and neither officer is labelled 'S151' anywhere in the paper. Email drafted, in that spirit: reconciliation leads (empty on both sides), then the temporal diff on the Sep-26 target rate, then the shape of the borrowing they're about to take on.

officer.subject: Your September borrowing decision, and where the curve went
officer.body:
Hi Abdul,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts ahead of Bromley's first PWLB drawdown. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Your February report is unusually explicit about the timing and the reasoning behind it, and this is offered in that spirit rather than as a critique.

The first thing worth saying is a reconciliation, because ours is a rare shape: we hold no PWLB loans for the London Borough of Bromley, matching the zero on your p.11 exactly. Bromley is one of only a handful of councils in this month's reading with no external debt at all. That makes the September decision unusual in the sector — most authorities we read are managing a book, not opening one.

On timing, the market has moved since the Q3 report went to Council. Your paragraph 7.1 targets first drawdown around September 2026, on the expectation that the 50-year PWLB rate would fall from approximately 5.91% in November to 5.4% by March 2026 and around 5.3% from September. Today's 50-year certainty rate is 6.27% — roughly 97 basis points above your September expectation, and 36 basis points above the November starting point you identified as the level to fall from. The rest of the long end has moved similarly against MUFG's 22 December forecast for September 2026: five-year 5.34% against 4.30% forecast, ten-year 5.83% against 4.90%, twenty-five year 6.46% against 5.60%. The strategy's own target-borrowing-rate table on p.14, set 11 August last year, targets 50-year at 5.20% by the end of Q2 2027 — that would require roughly 107 basis points off the long end in ten months. Bank Rate is 3.75% today with the one-year OIS around 4.11%, so the market is now pricing a hike into late 2026 or early 2027 rather than the cuts that framed the paper.

On the shape of what you're about to take on, the p.11 build-up totals £241.4m of drawdown by 31 March 2029 against £273m agreed in principle, and the ratio of financing costs to net revenue moves from zero to 2.2% inside three years. Your existing internal-borrowing position (about £63m at 31/03/26 on our arithmetic of CFR minus OLTL) essentially closes to zero over that period as PWLB replaces reserves — the paper's own trajectory rather than an inference. Worth noting that your £55m of local-authority lending sits at 4.30–4.75% across five borrowers, which is where the LA-to-LA market still prices inside the PWLB curve at every tenor today; short-dated fixed LA-to-LA is explicitly flagged by MUFG on p.14 for exactly that reason.

The pages that go with all this: today's rates at both fixings and the whole curve are at pwlbtoday.org/dashboard; the monthly sector breakdown at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity shows what everyone else has been drawing (July was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers, average 5.02%); and once loans are on the book, pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis prices any authority's PWLB position daily against the DMO's repayment curve. Our liability-benchmark pathway — five courses, interactive, built on live data — is directly relevant to a rising CFR that is about to be met externally, and to CIPFA's forthcoming Prudential and Treasury Code updates.

Free accounts for the whole team, and our 115 courses — officers and members, SONIA through to the Prudential Code — are free to local authorities until the end of September. Three that fit your position specifically: PWLB rates and the certainty discount, Cost of carry and internal borrowing (for the transition paragraph 7 describes), and Audit Committee Chair (Treasury) for the members who scrutinise this at ER&C PDS.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.
